messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT — elevated inference latency detected in prod (us-west-1). Metric: model-serving.p95_tokens > 1200ms for 6m. Triggered paging to #incidents.
Maria S.: I see it. Dash shows p50 ~ 180ms, p95 ~ 1.3s across the rtx-pool. Errors are low, just latency. Likely queuing/backpressure.
Jon P.: Confirming. Throughput is stable but queue depth increased on the 4xA100 tier. No obvious autoscaler events in the last 10m.
Alex R.: Dumping recent logs and tailing inference runtime:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:10Z INFO  batch_executor - batch_size=8 latency=130ms
2026-03-15T14:03:05Z WARN  kv_cache - backend_hitrate=0.12
2026-03-15T14:04:18Z ERROR kernel_fallback - fallback_count=3
2026-03-15T14:05:40Z INFO  scheduler - queue_len=460
```
Maria S.: Looks like KV cache hit rate tanked, fallback kernel spikes — that would amplify cost and push latency. Any recent rollout?
Lily T.: Product / deployments: no model changes in the last 24h. We did push a routing policy tweak to prefer low-cost variants for some requests at 13:50, but that should be transparent.
Alex R.: Reproducing locally is slow. Quick mitigation suggestions: 1) temporarily force routing to the high-perf model variant (pin) 2) increase dedicated pool by +2 nodes 3) disable the recent routing policy.
Jon P.: I'm going to pin traffic to model-x-large-hotfix1 and scale up the rtx-pool by 2 nodes. Doing change now.
Jon P.: Executed: pinned route to model-x-large-hotfix1, and submitted scale request to infra: `POST /infra/scale?pool=rtx-pool&delta=2` — infra accepted, expected capacity in ~2-3m.
IncidentBot: NOTE — statuspage update suggested: "Performance degradation affecting inference p95 in us-west-1. We are investigating and implementing mitigation steps. No data loss reported." Would you like me to post? (react with :white_check_mark: to post)
Lily T.: Draft for customers (CS):
"Hi — we are currently experiencing elevated latency for inference requests in our US-West region. Our engineers are actively investigating and applying mitigations. If you see higher-than-normal response times, please retry or route to a different region (us-east-1) where available. We will post updates here and on status.redwood.ai. — Redwood Inference Team"
CS Team: Please post that to affected midsize customers and include the status page link once IncidentBot posts. We'll prepare a targeted email if we see >10% error/impact on any account.
Maria S.: Infra reports nodes provisioning. Early telemetry: p95 dropped from 1.3s to 800ms after pin, queue length falling from 460 -> 180. KV cache still low though. Continuing to watch cache warming.
Alex R.: To help cache warm faster, we can: 1) replay a small sample of recent successful prefixes (non-PII) to populate KV, 2) temporarily relax per-tenant cache eviction to lengthen TTL. I can run a safe prefix-replay job now.
Jon P.: Go ahead, Alex. I'll keep an eye on autoscaler. If we don't hit p95 < 500ms in 10m, escalate to SRE lead for manual kernel optimization.
Alex R.: Started prefix-replay job (readonly, safe). Logs: `replay-job-id=kj-4910`. Monitoring hit-rate.
Maria S.: Update: after replay and scaling, p95 is trending ~420ms and queue is steady. Reactions: :thumbsup: Great job.
IncidentBot: ACTION LOGGED — mitigation steps: pinned to model-x-large-hotfix1, scaled rtx-pool +2, prefix-replay job kj-4910 started. Expected follow-up: monitor for 30m, roll back pin when cache stabilized.
Lily T.: Status page update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1907 — text mirrors draft. Also adding ETA: recovery in 10-30 minutes depending on cache warmup.
CS Team: Notifying top-20 customers now with template. Will escalate to account leads for any customers who report impact.
Sam O.: I'm taking over on-call from Jon in 15m. Jon, please hand off the context you want me to watch.
Jon P.: Handoff: watch p95 (model-serving.p95_tokens), queue_len, kv_cache.hitrate, and replay-job status. If p95 creeps above 700ms again, consider temporary regional routing to us-east-1 and open an incident severity call. Logs and runbook: `#eng-oncall/runbooks/latency-mitigation` (see section "cache-fallback-recovery").
Sam O.: Got it. I'll be on watch and will update every 10m. Thanks.
Maria S.: Final note: no data exfiltration or errors reported, only performance. Post-incident action items: investigate root cause of KV cache collapse (metrics, prefetch regression), add alert for kernel-fallback spikes, and review recent routing policy change.
IncidentBot: INCIDENT STATUS — Mitigated (partial). Current impact: elevated latency resolved to acceptable threshold in us-west-1. Follow-ups assigned. Thread closed for active paging; please re-open if latency regresses. :white_check_mark:
